title: Endoscopic transcanal repair of temporomandibular joint herniation into the external auditory canal: literature review
html: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) herniation into the external auditory canal is a rare condition associated with anterior canal wall defects, most commonly due to a patent foramen of Huschke, trauma, or infection. The clinical presentation is variable and often non-specific, which may lead to misdiagnosis. High-resolution computed tomography is crucial for accurate diagnosis and effective surgical planning. While open surgical repair remains standard, minimally invasive approaches have not been widely reported.
